function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity isn’t something that was “discovered” by a single person—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been observed and studied for millennia. Over time, many scientists and thinkers made key contributions that helped us understand and harness it:

| Era | Key Figures | Contributions |
|-----|-------------|---------------|
| Ancient Greece | Thales of Miletus | Noted static electricity from rubbing amber. |
| 17th–18th Century | William Gilbert, Otto von Guericke | Studied magnetism and static electricity. |
| 18th Century | Benjamin Franklin | Conducted kite experiment, coined “positive” and “negative” charges. |
| 19th Century | Alessandro Volta | Invented the voltaic pile (first battery). |
| 19th Century | Michael Faraday | Discovered electromagnetic induction. |
| 19th Century | James Clerk Maxwell | Unified electricity and magnetism into Maxwell’s equations. |

So while no single person “discovered” electricity, the cumulative work of many scientists over centuries led to our modern understanding and use of electrical phenomena.
